title: Rav Chana bar Hinda

paragraphs: So it is cited in the She’iltot, Miketz: he said in the name of Rabbi Pedat, in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, “Whoever sees a dream and is troubled should set it out before three.” The reading Hyman uses, cited as Bekhorot 55b, is Rav Huna bar Ami. The supplied notice ends “and so it cites there [1].”

notes.text: The supplied notice ends at “and so it cites there [1]”; its continuation and footnote are missing. Bekhorot 55b is retained as supplied, alongside the matching William Davidson digital Berakhot 55b Rav Huna bar Ami–Rabbi Pedat–Rabbi Yochanan chain. The supplied יפרטנו is translated “set it out”; the Bavli first has יפתרנו, “have it interpreted,” then revises this to יטיבנו, “have it ameliorated.” The incomplete source remains held.

On Hyman’s printed page (vol. II, p. 464), “and so it cites there” comes immediately before the separately headed Rav Chana bar Chimi notice. That notice concerns filling oneself with Torah or reciting the Shema before sleep. The She’iltot, Miketz 29:1, gives that teaching under Rav Chana bar Chimi and the dream teaching under Rav Chana bar Hinda. In Berakhot 14a the Torah teaching comes through Rav Acha, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. The inspected printed boundary has no [1] marker. Hyman prints Bekhorot 55b, while the matching Bavli dream passage is in Berakhot 55b.
